newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: About 600 girls circumcised in Sierra Leone ritual.
newsitem.headline: About 600 girls circumcised in Sierra Leone ritual.

text.p: A powerful women's secret society in Sierra Leone circumcised about 600 girls in a camp for displaced people and many have developed complications from the mass ritual, aid workers said on Sunday.
The Bondo Society, which promotes female circumcision in the West African country, carried out the ritual on Thursday in Grafton Camp in the eastern suburbs of Freetown, they said.

Health workers said about 100 of the girls, who are aged between eight and 15, were suffering severe complications. The practice involves the removal of the clitoris with unsterilised knives or other objects, with no form of anesthesia.

"Some are suffering from profuse bleeding and other attendant illnesses of female circumcision," a health worker said. The medical charity Medecins Sans Frontieres had put the most serious cases in intensive care.

State radio broadcast an official statement on Sunday denying what it said were reports that the camp circumcisions were sanctioned by First Lady Patricia Kabbah, the Christian wife of Moslem President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah.
"The First Lady never forced anybody to be circumcised against their will," the radio said.
Anti-circumcision campaigners have accused President Kabbah of condoning the traditional practice that affects an estimated 90 percent of Sierra Leonean women.

The president angered activists last year when he received a group of Bondo women who staged a noisy demonstration in favour of female circumcision, an essential part of coming-of-age rituals in many traditional African societies.
In the runup to elections that brought Kabbah to power last March, Bondo women pledged to vote for Kabbah in return for his promise to check the anti-circumcision lobby, activists say.
The Grafton girls have not indicated they were forcibly circumcised but several parents told reporters they had been approached by Bondo women in the name of Mrs Kabbah.
Local newspapers reported that the First Lady had provided food and other help for the girls since their initiation. Government spokesmen have not denied this.
